concepts.name: Learned medicine
concepts.summary: A body of diagnosis, prognosis and remedies that specialists record, teach and hand on as a discipline.

concepts.name: Hospital
concepts.summary: A permanent institution where the sick are lodged and treated by attendants and physicians.

concepts.name: Oral rehydration therapy
concepts.summary: Replacing the fluid lost in diarrhoea by drinking a measured solution of glucose and salts.

concepts.name: Randomised controlled trial
concepts.summary: Testing a treatment by allotting patients at random to receive it or not and comparing the outcomes.

concepts.name: Trepanation
concepts.summary: Cutting an opening in the skull of a living person who then survives.

concepts.name: Reconstructive surgery
concepts.summary: Rebuilding a damaged part of the body by moving the patient's own living tissue.

concepts.name: General anaesthesia
concepts.summary: Making a patient reversibly unconscious and free of pain so that surgery can be done.

concepts.name: Coca leaf use
concepts.summary: Chewing coca leaves with an alkali to release a stimulant that dulls hunger, fatigue and pain.

concepts.name: Cinchona bark against malaria
concepts.summary: Treating malarial fever with the bark of the cinchona tree or the quinine extracted from it.

concepts.name: Isolation of a drug's active principle
concepts.summary: Extracting the pure active compound from a medicinal plant so that it can be dosed exactly.

concepts.name: Antimicrobial chemotherapy
concepts.summary: Curing an infection with a synthetic chemical designed to kill the microbe and spare the patient.

concepts.name: Insulin therapy
concepts.summary: Keeping people with diabetes alive by injecting insulin extracted or made outside the body.

concepts.name: Artemisinin against malaria
concepts.summary: Treating malaria with artemisinin, the active compound of sweet wormwood, and drugs derived from it.

concepts.name: Smallpox inoculation
concepts.summary: Deliberately giving a healthy person a mild case of smallpox with matter from a patient, to protect against the deadly natural disease.

concepts.name: Laboratory-made vaccine
concepts.summary: Protecting against a disease with a microbe that has been deliberately weakened or killed in the laboratory.

concepts.name: Virus vaccine from cell culture
concepts.summary: Growing a virus in cultured cells in quantity so that a vaccine can be made from it.

concepts.name: Clonal selection theory of immunity
concepts.summary: The explanation that each immune cell makes one antibody and that an infection selects and multiplies the cells that fit it.

concepts.name: Waterborne transmission of disease
concepts.summary: The finding that some epidemic diseases spread through drinking water fouled by the wastes of the sick.

concepts.name: Insect transmission of disease
concepts.summary: The finding that biting insects carry certain diseases from one person to the next.

concepts.name: Dietary deficiency disease
concepts.summary: The finding that some diseases come from the lack of a trace substance in food, not from an infection or poison.

concepts.name: Smoking as a cause of disease
concepts.summary: The demonstration from population studies that smoking tobacco causes lung cancer and other fatal diseases.

concepts.name: Quarantine
concepts.summary: Holding arriving people, ships and goods apart for a fixed period so that an epidemic disease cannot enter.

concepts.name: Citywide sewerage
concepts.summary: A planned network of drains that carries household waste water out of a whole city.

concepts.name: Disinfection of public drinking water
concepts.summary: Treating a town's piped water continuously with a chemical that kills the germs in it.

concepts.name: Eradication of a human disease
concepts.summary: Ending all natural transmission of an infectious disease everywhere, so that it no longer exists outside laboratories.

concepts.name: Spectacles
concepts.summary: Lenses worn before the eyes to correct poor sight.

concepts.name: Intensive care with mechanical ventilation
concepts.summary: Keeping critically ill patients alive by breathing for them through the windpipe under constant watch in a dedicated ward.

concepts.name: Anatomy from human dissection
concepts.summary: Learning the structure of the human body by systematically cutting open and describing the dead.

concepts.name: Circulation of the blood
concepts.summary: The finding that the heart pumps the blood round the body in a closed circuit.

concepts.name: Caesarean section
concepts.summary: Delivering a child through a cut in the abdomen and womb so that mother and child both live.

concepts.name: Hormonal contraception
concepts.summary: Preventing pregnancy with synthetic hormones that stop ovulation.

concepts.name: Meditation
concepts.summary: A taught discipline of training attention and calming the mind through sustained practice.

concepts.name: Experimental psychology
concepts.summary: Studying perception, memory and thought by measurement and controlled experiment.

concepts.name: Psychotherapy
concepts.summary: Treating mental distress through a structured course of conversation with a trained practitioner.

concepts.name: Drug treatment of mental illness
concepts.summary: Relieving the symptoms of a major mental illness with a drug that acts on them specifically, not by sedation alone.

concepts.name: Clothing
concepts.summary: Covering the body with worked skins or other materials for warmth and protection.

concepts.name: Sewing with the eyed needle
concepts.summary: Stitching skins into close-fitting garments with a needle that carries its thread through an eye.

concepts.name: Tailored polar clothing
concepts.summary: Layered, fitted and waterproof-seamed skin garments that let people live and hunt through polar winters.

concepts.name: Personal ornament
concepts.summary: Wearing made objects such as beads on the body to mark identity, standing or belonging.

concepts.name: Tattooing
concepts.summary: Marking the skin permanently by putting pigment beneath it.

concepts.name: Cosmetics
concepts.summary: Prepared paints, salves and scents made and put on the face and body as a regular habit.

concepts.name: Mirror
concepts.summary: A surface polished or coated so that a person can see their own reflection.

concepts.name: Lamp
concepts.summary: A vessel that burns fat or oil on a wick to give portable, lasting light.

concepts.name: Underfloor heating
concepts.summary: Warming a room by leading the hot gases of a fire through channels beneath its floor.

concepts.name: Hammock
concepts.summary: A bed of netting or cloth slung between two supports.

concepts.name: Washing machine
concepts.summary: A powered machine that washes household laundry.

concepts.name: Soap
concepts.summary: A cleansing substance made by boiling fats or oils with an alkali.

concepts.name: Sweat bath
concepts.summary: A closed room or lodge heated with fire or hot stones in which people sweat and wash.

concepts.name: Flush toilet
concepts.summary: A toilet that washes waste away with water and seals the drain against foul air.

concepts.name: Toothbrush
concepts.summary: A handled brush of bristles for cleaning the teeth.

concepts.name: Disposable menstrual products
concepts.summary: Manufactured absorbent pads or tampons that are used once and thrown away.
